channel.title: spawnpoint blog
channel.description: Notes from spawnpoint on small software.

item.title: spawnpoint vs Base44 for a team's apps
item.description: On spawnpoint every app starts private, building is not metered, and the people you share an app with open it with an email code and no account. Base44 needs a paid plan for a private app and charges credits for each change its AI makes.

item.title: spawnpoint vs Vercel for the apps your team builds with AI
item.description: Vercel suits engineers shipping a product to the public. spawnpoint suits the small apps people across a company build with a coding agent and share with coworkers, who open them with an email code and no account.

item.title: When a Claude artifact should become a spawnpoint app
item.description: Keep an artifact when it is a page for people who use Claude. Move it to spawnpoint when it needs a server, more saved data, or viewers without a Claude account, and do it from the same chat.

item.title: spawnpoint vs Retool for internal tools
item.description: Retool builds internal tools in its own editor and bills every person who uses them. spawnpoint puts the apps your people build with Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor online, and the people you share them with open them free.

item.title: spawnpoint vs Replit for a team's apps
item.description: Replit is an editor, an agent, and publishing in one product, paid for in credits. spawnpoint puts the apps your team builds with Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor online for one flat price, shared with people who need no account.

item.title: spawnpoint vs Lovable for a team's apps
item.description: Lovable builds and publishes apps in its own editor. spawnpoint puts the apps your team builds with the coding agent it already uses online, and the people you share them with need no account.

item.title: How to share Claude Code skills and MCP servers with your whole team
item.description: Publish your skills and deploy your MCP servers to a spawnpoint team. Every member's agent sees the team's skills, and one install line adds the team's MCP servers and skills to each person's Claude Code or Codex.

item.title: How to share an app with a few people without making them sign up
item.description: On spawnpoint, share the app with their email address. They open the link and type a one-time code from their inbox. Nobody makes an account, and nobody you did not share with can open the app.

item.title: How to put an app you built with Claude Code online
item.description: Install spawnpoint once, sign in once, and tell Claude Code to deploy. A minute or two later it gives you a private link that stays online after you close your laptop. The same works in Codex, Cursor, Copilot, and a Claude chat.

item.title: Where should the apps your team builds with AI live?
item.description: In one place the whole company can open and owns, such as a spawnpoint team. Most of them live on one person's laptop today. Here is how a team changes that.

item.title: We built our treg-powered CRM on spawnpoint
item.description: The CRM we use to find spawnpoint's own customers finds people through treg and runs on spawnpoint as a Node server, a Postgres database, an always-on Discord bot, and an open AI model. Claude Code built it and put it online in about fifteen minutes.

item.title: You can spawn AI apps now
item.description: spawnpoint now runs open-source AI models on its own servers. Your app can chat, summarize, read images, search your documents, and make quick typed decisions, with the model calls staying inside spawnpoint.

item.title: Your apps can now keep their data and files
item.description: A spawnpoint app can now have its own database and its own file storage, and your agent adds them when the app needs them.

item.title: Bigger apps now go live faster
item.description: We changed how spawnpoint puts an app onto the computer it runs on. An app with 4 MB of files now goes live in 72 seconds instead of 93.

item.title: What small software is
item.description: Software for one purpose or a few people, which an AI agent can now write in an afternoon, and the four things it needs once it works.
